targets.target: Twitch OAuth token validation and refresh
findings: Third-party OAuth clients must validate at startup and hourly thereafter.

A token is definitively invalid when validation returns HTTP 401; revoked/expired access tokens also produce 401 on API calls. An Authorization Code refresh token can obtain a replacement user access token without new consent until that refresh authorization itself is invalid.
Network failures and service failures do not prove token revocation. Invalid refresh token is a confirmed consent problem; transient transport/5xx/429 refresh failures must remain recoverable.
Authorization Code user refresh can return a rotated refresh token, which must be saved safely with the access token.
implications: Do not mark reconnect_required from a generic thrown exception; classify typed HTTP 401 separately from transport, timeout, 429, and server failures. A 401 access-token validation should try the saved refresh token before deciding whether user consent is required.
Continue the hourly validation obligation even when an earlier attempt was transiently unavailable, using bounded retry scheduling.
Only persist new refresh credentials after receiving a successful refresh response; retain last valid durable credentials on transient failures.

findings: RefreshingAuthProvider exposes refresh and refresh-failure callbacks; 8.2.0 getTokenInfo maps HTTP 401 to InvalidTokenError but propagates other HTTP/transport errors.
The installed EventSubWsSocket uses the supplied reconnect_url for Twitch session_reconnect and keeps subscriptions on the replacement session.

The installed PersistentConnection starts with three retry attempts for an explicit initial connection; after an established connection drops, it selects persistent retry with capped Fibonacci delays. The application currently does not supervise a fresh startup after initial exhaustion.
Twurple emits disconnect and ready callbacks on a new socket session; application reconciliation currently relies on observing a disconnect before the next ready callback.
implications: Preserve Twurple's built-in session migration instead of adding a competing WebSocket connection loop.
Add application-level recoverable initialization supervision for validation/eligibility failures and handle initial socket retry exhaustion if the installed API does not continue it.
Use the disconnect/ready lifecycle or a narrow supervisor callback to reconcile after a genuine dropped session; do not treat Twitch's seamless session_reconnect as a dropped-event gap.

targets.target: Existing integration, durable workers, health, and OAuth state
findings: FND-4 already covers OAuth, token persistence, hourly validation, initial reconciliation, and recovery after EventSub reconnect callbacks. It does not cover transient startup retry classification or automatic reconstruction after validation/eligibility initialization failure.
FND-5 already provides durable outbox records and retry behavior; runtime workers report idle if no Twitch adapter exists. Those records are not deleted by Twitch integration shutdown.
The health contract already has connecting, reconciling, degraded, and reconnect_required states; the panel has status localization and a manual reconnect action.

At startup, createRefreshingAuthRuntime currently marks reconnect_required for every thrown validation error; eligibility lookup failure stops the auth runtime and leaves eligibility_unknown with no retry supervisor.
implications: OPS-8 extends the FND-4 integration lifecycle and tests rather than reimplementing token/reconciliation/outbox mechanics.
Keep the current local status projections and provide an explicit retrying/recovering state if the existing states cannot distinguish transient recovery adequately.
Workers may keep durable pending rows while no adapter is available, but ensure they are restarted/resumed when the integration is restored.

decision: Implement a single cancellable integration supervisor around saved credential startup and post-failure recovery. Keep OAuth state and existing durable data unchanged. Treat definitive authentication/scope failure as reconnect_required and transient errors as degraded/retrying. Use Twurple 8.2.0's native WebSocket migration/reconnection and reconcile when a genuinely new session follows disconnection.
liveVerification: Not performed. No live Twitch credentials or requests were used for this planning research.
